sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (4th Supp.) and the Act respecting the regulation of certain activities in the field of money laundering and terrorist financing (Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Identity (Passport or National ID)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FINTRAC guidelines, OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated List, and Canadian Sanctions List

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in French; English names permitted with French translation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Filing an administrative appeal with the Minister of Economy and Innovation within 30 days of notice of rejection

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for registered office address in Quebec for most industries including wholesale trading
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for standard wholesale entities; unannounced inspections occur only in cases of suspected non-compliance or AML red flags

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and UBO identification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border corporate setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of limited partnership registration and filing
Registered office address and compliance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Quebec registered office

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ) arts. 2236-2241 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, ss. 1, 15-20 (obligatory registration); Regulation respecting the Registraire des entreprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, r. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec Enterprise Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement. Inbound contributions must be wired to a Canadian financial institution and are subject to FINTRAC client identification and PCMLTFA record-keeping. No Quebec statute prescribes an escrow account; escrow arrangements may be adopted contractually for conditional closing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the undersigned limited partners to 100 limited partnership units set out in Schedule A is accepted, and the General Partner is authorized to issue exchangeable limited partnership units and record contributions accordingly; AND RESOLVED, that the registered office and head office of the Partnership shall be established at [address], Québec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec shall be appointed to record the same; AND RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed as senior officers and authorized representatives of the General Partner, each to act singly, for opening bank accounts, signing the declaration of registration and commercial contracts; AND RESOLVED, that the partnership agreement be ratified and the fiscal year-end fixed at December 31 of each year.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain enterprise name clearance and REQ eligibility confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Centre de services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request through the REQ online portal. The proposed limited partnership name must include 'société en commandite' (s.e.c.) or 'limited partnership' (L.P.) and must be predominantly French unless a legal exception applies. Obtain the Avis de disponibilité de nom (name availability certificate), valid for 180 days. After clearance, reserve the name via the same portal and receive the reservation number for the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Name search request form
General partner's authorization to make the name application
Supporting trademark or registered name documents, if any
Power of attorney if filed by an external representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects the proposed name on grounds of similarity or misleading connotation, file a request for administrative revision under s. 20 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, or amend the name to a distinctive French-language corporate designation and re-submit without prejudice to the existing reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and ratify the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner's records – notarial or private written instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the limited partnership agreement by the General Partner and all limited partners. The agreement must state the partnership's name, registered office address, the identity of the general partner, the capital commitments of each limited partner, the nature of contributions, profit-sharing ratios, withdrawal and transfer conditions, and the authority of the General Partner. The instrument may be a private deed; however, an English or French version must be available for REQ inspection and bank onboarding. Keep the original executed copy in the corporate binder.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Schedule A of limited partners and capital contributions
Consent and KYC documents of each limited partner
General partner's certificate of corporate authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a limited partner objects to a term during execution, execute an amending rider signed by all partners. If any partner's KYC dossier is incomplete, suspend the subscription and request certified identity and source-of-funds documentation from the partner within 5 business days before the REQ filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the declaration of registration and obtain NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Registrations Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ online portal and file the Déclaration d'immatriculation. Provide all particulars required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, including the limited partnership name, REQ name reservation reference, registered office address in Québec, general partner and limited partner particulars, principal place of business, sector of activity (NAICS 423430), and start date. Pay the filing fee by credit card or approved transfer. Upon successful processing, REQ will issue an Attestation d'immatriculation and assign a Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Completed declaration of registration form
Avis de disponibilité de nom (name availability certificate)
Limited partnership agreement (review copy, if requested)
General partner's authorization resolution
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or notarial deed)
Payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a query or inspection notice, respond within 10 days with an attestation of identity for each partner and a certified copy of the partnership agreement. If the declaration is refused for missing particulars, exercise the curative right under s. 22 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises by filing a supplementary declaration and paying the standard amendment fee, or request an administrative review if the refusal is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register federal and provincial tax accounts with CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain a Business Number (BN) under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act for GST/HST. Then complete the Revenu Québec registration, using the NEQ from step 3, to obtain a QST (taxe de vente du Québec) registration and accounts for employer payroll, if applicable. For international wholesale, confirm zero-rated treatment of exported computer chips and backup documentation under Excise Tax Act s. 21(2).
required_dossiers: Attestation d'immatriculation or NEQ confirmation
CRA Business Registration Online form (RC1 or online profile)
Revenu Québec 'Demande d'inscription au fichier de la clientèle' form
List of partnerships officers and general partner directors
Bank account statement or confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA delays BN issuance due to partner KYC, escalate via the CRA Business Window by filing a service request with reference documents. If Revenu Québec requests additional information regarding non-resident limited partners, submit a completed NR6 or withholding certification for non-resident partners and obtain a Revenu Québec clearance letter before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal and cross-border trade registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permit office and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) – CARM
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the limited partnership maintains a warehouse or commercial office, verify municipal zoning and obtain a business occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) from the competent city or borough. For international trade of SSD and CPU chips, open a CBSA Customs Account through the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal, apply for an import/export program account, and obtain a carrier/inward processing reference if bonded movements are needed. Confirm the partnership's goods fall under HS 8473/8471 for chips and modules.
required_dossiers: Municipal zoning and occupancy permit application
Lease agreement or ownership proof
Structural load compliance for storage racks (if warehouse)
CBSA Customs Account application and security questionnaire
Importer/exporter identity documents and financial statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused for lack of structural compliance, obtain an engineering condition report and apply for a minor variance or conditional permit through the municipal council of arbitration. If the CBSA party screening triggers enhanced verification, submit a board resolution confirming the beneficial ownership of the limited partnership and the passport of each authorized agent, requesting an expedited review within 15 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) – Direction des secteurs industriels
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for ISIC 4651 wholesale trade of solid-state drives and server processors under Quebec law; where premises are occupied, only a municipal commercial occupancy permit and environmental compliance obligations apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (non-industrial wholesale distribution; no intensive extraction, manufacturing or central combustion process requiring an EIA under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or regulated atmospheric emissions are anticipated. If an emergency standby generator is installed, comply with the Clean Air Act (CQLR c. Q-2) and municipal noise limits. Waste electrical and electronic equipment, including end-of-life SSD/CPU units, must be handled under the Regulation respecting the recovery of electronic products (CQLR c. E-12.1, r. 2) and the Regulation respecting the landfilling and incineration of residual materials. Municipal sewer discharge limits apply only to sanitary effluent from office/warehouse facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the competent municipal fire safety service under the Quebec Building Code (CQLR c. B-1.1) and the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c. S-3.4). Structural load inspection is mandatory for warehouse racking systems and high-density storage; a licensed engineer must certify all load-bearing capacity and anchoring for seismic safety. Occupational clearance from the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) is required for workforce health and safety coverage, including a workplace risk assessment, ventilation adequacy for electronics storage, and first-aid protocols.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada has no separate foreign-exchange-control administration. Exchange and payment compliance is administered through the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and Global Affairs Canada for export/import permit matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible, free-floating Canadian dollar and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are generally unrestricted with no exchange control permits required. Profit and capital remittances from a Quebec Limited Partnership to a non-resident limited partner may proceed freely, but federal Part XIII withholding tax and corresponding Quebec non-resident withholding tax may apply to distributions, including partnership allocations taxable in Canada; treaty relief is available through Canada Revenue Agency Form NR301 or equivalent evidence. Investment Canada Act filing thresholds may apply to large non-resident capital injections into a Canadian business, but passive limited-partner investment below applicable net-benefit review thresholds is not typically blocked.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be maintained in any freely convertible currency. The Income Tax Act nonetheless requires Canadian tax records and returns to be prepared in Canadian dollars, with foreign-denominated amounts translated at an acceptable exchange rate. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), financial institutions must report and retain records for international electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more, and the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA) may require an export permit for controlled goods; current-generation commercial SSD/CPU wholesale products are generally not subject to export controls unless designed for military, encryption, or advanced-computing end-uses, and an Export Control List classification assessment should be documented.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium, conditional. An offshore digital EMI cannot operate as a deposit-taking institution in Canada unless it is regulated as a bank under the Bank Act or is registered as a money-services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, where applicable, licensed by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) in Quebec. Unlicensed offshore EMIs cannot clear CAD wires directly, cannot hold settlement funds in Canada, and are generally not acceptable as a primary treasury rail. A compliant approach is to use a Schedule I Canadian bank for the Quebec LP operating and escrow accounts, with the offshore EMI used only as a front-end customer interface provided all fiat settlement flows are routed through a Canadian licensed institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks generally permit remote corporate account opening using electronic identity verification, video interviews, and digital execution of account documents; however, at least one controlling general partner or authorized signatory is normally required to complete a live compliance interview, either physically at a Canadian branch or through an approved secure video call, before account activation. A Quebec Limited Partnership will also be required to provide its deed of establishment, certificate of registration, general partner identification, and a full beneficial-ownership schedule. Some banks impose a physical meeting for the general partner when the partnership has non-resident limited partners or medium-risk trade activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident passive limited partners prevents timely identification of beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute Quebec limited-partnership declaration, provide up-to-date Register of Limited Partners, identify every person holding 25% or more of partnership interests, provide a detailed organizational chart, copy of the limited partnership agreement, government-issued photo ID and proof of address for the general partner and each material beneficial owner, and a written confirmation that no undisclosed settlor or nominee holds partnership interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border spot semiconductor trading appears inconsistent with stated sales volumes, triggers high-velocity outbound wire activity, or involves jurisdictions on enhanced-watch lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide contractual sale and purchase agreements, commercial invoices, packing lists, airway bills or bills of lading, customs declarations, underlying SSD/CPU serial or lot data, independent escrow or inspection terms, end-customer details, source-of-funds explanations, and six to twelve months of projected transaction flow with estimated amounts and counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use product classification risk: wholesale brokers of SSD/CPU chips may inadvertently trade items subject to export controls, sanctions, or military end-use restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an EIPA/Export Control List classification memo, product technical datasheets, manufacturer compliance attestations, end-user and end-use certificates, distributor agreements, a notarized confirmation that the buyer is not a restricted/embargoed party, internal sanctions screening results, and a written policy prohibiting military, nuclear, or strategic end-use without Global Affairs Canada authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow inspection wire arrangements create third-party payment scenarios in which funds move before title is fully verified, raising money-laundering layering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full escrow agreement, independent inspection company engagement letter, inspection certificate process documentation, proof of title transfer or customs release, matching purchase and sale orders, legal entity identifiers of all parties, and confirmation that no cash, crypto, or unlicensed payment intermediary is involved in settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident limited partners should be routed by SWIFT MT103 / ISO 20022 high-value payment to the Quebec LP's Canadian operational or capital escrow account held at a Schedule I bank. Field 70 remittance information should state clearly: 'LP capital contribution — Quebec Limited Partnership — wholesale SSD/CPU distribution' and reference the dated limited partnership agreement. Canadian banks will require source-of-wealth documentation, confirmation of the Investment Canada Act status, source of funds, and proof of identity of the remitting limited partner. International EFTs of C$10,000 or more are recorded and may trigger FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution; no foreign-exchange permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 direct correspondent wires for open-account settlement and irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 for escrow/inspection transactions. CAD clearing should occur through Payments Canada settlement systems via the Canadian bank, while USD clearing can be executed through the bank's US correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS). The 'Escrow_Inspection_Wire' rail should be implemented by instructing the bank to release funds only upon presentation of an inspection certificate, warehouse receipt, or customs release matching the negotiated trade terms. MT700/MT103 fields must reference the underlying commercial invoice, LC number, and ISIC 4651 trade description. Crypto rails and unlicensed digital payment intermediaries are not permitted as formal treasury settlement channels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Canadian-dollar forward contracts with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or authorized financial institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the counterparty cannot physically settle CAD; otherwise the onshore deliverable CAD forward market is preferred
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps hedging USD/CAD cash flows
Vanilla FX options and FX collars on USD/CAD with an authorized derivatives counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (ALPE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due no later than the last day of the month following the month containing the REQ registration anniversary; must be renewed within each 12-month cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penal fine of CAD 200 to CAD 2,500 per offence for an enterprise and up to CAD 10,000 for a legal person; registration is administratively struck off (radiation) after five consecutive years without filing, which causes loss of legal publicity and may remove the limited partners' liability protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 partner slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); T5013 slips must be provided to partners and filed with CRA by March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 per return under ITA section 162(7), doubled on second offence; failure to file T5013 slips attracts additional penalties; administrative strike-off does not apply but persistent non-filing triggers CRA compliance actions and partnership audit risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Return and RL-15 Relevés (Québec partnership information filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); RL-15 slips must be sent to partners and filed with Revenu Québec by the end of February of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 per return; repeated non-filing may lead to penal proceedings and administrative assessments under Quebec tax legislation, though registration strike-off is not applicable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a non-reporting Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec or the ALPE. A certified independent audit becomes compulsory if (i) the partnership agreement or a financing/credit instrument requires audited financial statements, (ii) the LP or any general partner becomes a reporting issuer under the Québec Securities Act or NI 51-102, or (iii) an external counterparty, escrow bank, or the Canada Revenue Agency imposes an audited-financial-statement condition. For a private wholesale trading LP below these triggers, a review engagement is generally sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) at the preparer's election; ASPE is the prevalent local GAAP for a private wholesale LP. Financial records must support the T5013 and TP-600 information returns, and each fiscal period must not exceed 12 months without tax-authority authorization.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec limited partnerships are not subject to a separate annual UBO declaration to the REQ; the annual declaration confines disclosure to the general partner identification, registered office, and principal establishment. Any transfer of limited partnership units or change in general partner must be recorded in the internal ownership ledger and reflected via an amending declaration (déclaration modificative) to the REQ within the required delay. For anti-money-laundering purposes under the PCMLTFA and Québec FPPQ guidance, the LP must complete KYC and beneficial-ownership verification at admission and at each unit transfer, retaining written confirmations; the statutory significant-control register regime applies to corporations under the QBCA and is not applicable to LPs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (unit-holdings and transfer log)
Register of General Partners (identification, term, and resignation log)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, consents, and declaration filing log)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 80–300 per year (CAD 110–410) for professional registered-office or registered-agent services in Quebec, including preparation and filing of the annual declaration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,500 (CAD 5,000–15,000) for a certified audit; USD 1,500–3,000 (CAD 2,000–4,000) for a review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal + Quebec general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec); the LP itself is a flow-through entity and does not pay entity-level corporate income tax unless the partners jointly elect to be treated as a corporation under Quebec law.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for wholesale distribution of SSD/CPU chips. Canadian-controlled private corporate partners may access the federal small business deduction (9% federal, plus Quebec SMB reduction) provided they meet the CCPC and passive-income limits. Manufacturing and processing profits may attract a reduced Quebec rate, but ISIC 4651 wholesale brokerage does not qualify as M&P activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (CRA electronic filing via XML/Web Forms; Business Registration Online gateway)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the partnership's fiscal period end (December 31 year-end → June 30 filing deadline).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the same period end as the LP's accounting year. For non-resident partners with a different home-country fiscal year, the Canadian period governs for T5013 reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income of the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source gross revenue from wholesale SSD/CPU trading, including open-market commissions and escrow settlement amounts. Cost of goods sold is not netted at this field.
Claim only Canadian arm's-length expenses (freight, storage, inspection, customs bonds). Any related-party service or procurement charges must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income (loss) of the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate net income to each partner on Schedule 50 and issue T5013 slips. Non-resident partners must report their allocated share in Canada, subject to treaty or section 218 election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident partner's share of taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any partner is a non-resident corporation, disclose the share on Schedule 50 to trigger Part XIII remittance or election under section 218. Failure to disclose creates withholding exposure and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a T5013 return within the deadline incurs a penalty under subsection 162(1) of the Income Tax Act: CAD 25 per day, maximum CAD 2,500. Failure to issue T5013 slips or file the summary may add CAD 100 per slip plus CAD 50 per day, capped at CAD 100,000. A knowingly false return triggers gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: CO-1028 Partnership Return (Revenu Québec e-Transmit service)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the partnership's fiscal period end, aligned with the federal T5013 deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same year-end as the federal T5013 to avoid mismatched allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income or loss allocated to each Quebec-resident partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, only report the portion of income derived from Canadian sources that is taxable in Quebec; if the non-resident has no permanent establishment in Quebec, the treaty may exempt the allocation.
Enter the Part XIII or section 218 withholding remitted to Revenu Québec; attach a copy of the remittance vouchers and the non-resident partner's certificate of residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under the Quebec Taxation Act: CAD 25 per day, maximum CAD 2,500, plus an additional 10% penalty on any unpaid Quebec tax if the CO-1028 is filed more than 12 months late. Misrepresentations may attract a 50% penalty under section 1049 of the Quebec Taxation Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner claiming a reduced rate under an applicable tax treaty must: (1) obtain a valid certificate of residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US residents, or equivalent foreign TRC) containing the partner's TIN; (2) provide the LP with a Form NR301 or NR302 and a treaty-based disclosure letter before each distribution; (3) execute a section 218 election to file a Canadian Part I return, permitting a net-basis filing and refund of excess withholding if the treaty allocates the income to a permanent establishment; and (4) retain documentation to prove no PE in Canada (Canada-US treaty Article V) and no use of a DISE/limitation-of-benefits mismatch for treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: interest 25%, royalties 25%. Under Canada's tax treaties, arm's-length interest is reduced to 0% (e.g., Canada-US treaty Article XI) or up to 10% for non-arm's-length; patent/software royalties are reduced to 10% for most treaty partners, with some cultural royalties at 5%. For a wholesale LP purchasing chips from non-resident related sellers, embedded royalties for IP in SSD/CPU firmware must be separately identified and subjected to WHT unless the transaction is a complete goods sale at arm's length. Non-treaty jurisdictions remain at the 25% statutory rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 gross annual revenue and/or CAD 5,000,000 aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transaction value (CRA administrative safe harbour); for a wholesale LP, any related-party procurement of SSD/CPU inventory from a non-resident parent or supplier will breach this threshold, requiring preparation of a Local File (Schedule 91) and Master File within 3 months after the filing deadline.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as found in the UAE or other OFC jurisdictions. Instead, the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 ITA) and Quebec's anti-avoidance rule (section 24.0.1 of the Taxation Act) require genuine commercial purpose and actual economic substance. A QC LP that merely issues invoices from a briefcase office, holds no inventory, performs no operational control, and streams profits to a related non-resident distributor is exposed to GAAR reassessment, treaty residency denial under MLI Article 29 (LOB), and penalties. To maintain substance, the LP must demonstrate real procurement negotiations, inspection responsibilities, freight/payment risk, and independent decision-making from Quebec.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Income Tax Act, Part XV)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly unreporting SSD/CPU wholesale income through a tiered LP structure, issuing backdated escrow invoices, or instructing clients to pay a non-resident shell instead of the QC LP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under section 239(1) of the Income Tax Act: fine of 50%–200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years, for each count. Civil gross negligence penalty under subsection 163(2) adds 50% of the understated tax. Revenu Québec has parallel authority under sections 1060–1066 of the Taxation Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners who participate in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid amounts under subsection 227.1 ITA, plus personal fines and seizure of family assets. Travel bans under the PCTFA (Crim. Code s.462.33) may be issued during cross-border tax money laundering investigations; imprisonment is available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating the QC LP purely as a paper entity to route chip resale profits to a Hong Kong or Emirates affiliate with no employees, inventory, or operational control in Quebec, and relying on a divided profit margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The court may apply section 245 GAAR to invalidate the tax benefit and reassess on a substance-over-form basis; a penalty of up to 25% of the recharacterized benefit may be imposed under subsection 245(3). Revenu Québec may apply the same doctrine under s.24.0.2 of the Taxation Act. If tax evasion is proven, criminal sanctions as above may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the LP is a non-arm's-length sham; directors of the general partner are personally liable under Article 1457 of the Civil Code of Quebec for restoring taxes and damages, and may be subject to administrative penalties and prohibition orders issued by the CRA under the Voluntary Disclosures Program when attempting to regularize.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting third-party wire transfers from unknown beneficial owners, facilitating payments through unregistered money service intermediaries, failing to verify the manufacturer or importer's export licence, or omitting STR filings for high-value SSD chip transactions linked to sanctioned jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, a legal person can be fined up to CAD 2,000,000 per violation of the compliance program, reporting, or record-keeping obligations. Criminal laundering under Criminal Code section 462.31 carries imprisonment up to 10 years and forfeiture of all trading proceeds and any property derived from the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners who knowingly aid laundering or knowingly fail to prevent it are treated as parties to the offence under Criminal Code section 21, exposing them to 10-year imprisonment, personal fines, and an asset seizure order. FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties may also be issued directly against individual directors, reaching up to CAD 500,000 per contravention.
